answer: An agent market for meadow illustrations made with sable pigment allocates subsidized jobs by lottery over burn receipts, not account names. Each irreversibly burned coin buys one ticket bound to a key and round; validators reject reused receipts. A public random draw selects tickets only after purchases close. Dividing 100 tickets among 1,000 aliases leaves the same total chance of selection. More influence requires destroying more coins; this prices out free identity multiplication but cannot exclude a wealthy attacker.
